cim: EU leaders set for Dublin artificial intelligence summit
cim_eredeti: EU leaders set for Dublin artificial intelligence summit
szoveg_eredeti:
Discussions will look at how AI in Europe can compete with the US and China, as well as other key issues such as funding, security and red tape.

Leaders of the European Union will today (13 November) convene in Dublin for an inaugural summit on artificial intelligence.

In an invitation letter meant for EU leaders and issued last week, European Council president Antonio Costa said, “Given the rapid pace of AI ​development, I believe that a first dedicated discussion, at leaders’ level, is now needed on the ​opportunities presented by AI, as well as on its transformative effect on our economies and societies.”

The purpose of the meeting is to discuss how AI in Europe can compete with the US and China, as well as to address other key issues such as funding, security and red tape.

Among the speakers at the event will be Arthur Mensch, the head of Mistral AI and Geoffrey Hinton, the ‘Godfather of AI’.

According to France24, Mensch will explore the further development of European artificial intelligence, as well as how the technology can give a boost to Europe’s economy.

Reuters explained, in a letter ahead of the talks, representatives from Estonia and Finland said Europe must “establish EU-level arrangements for responding to serious AI incidents”. Additionally, they called for the development of advanced AI that could be responsibly governed.

Outside of AI, Leaders in attendance are also likely to discuss Ukraine, which has been added to the summit’s agenda. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have flown into Dublin to meet Ukraine’s President, Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

The summit is occurring at the same time as the recent revelation that Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang has been having an extra-marital affair with an alleged Chinese Spy. Huang has since resigned from his position, with chief financial officer Colette Kress announced as the company’s interim CEO.
